statement: Let an unlocking mask be any length-n binary list L' with L'[i] <= locked[i] for every 0 <= i < n. Let Sortable(nums,L') mean that there is a finite sequence of arrays a_0,...,a_k such that a_0 = nums, a_k is nondecreasing (a_k[i] <= a_k[i+1] for every 0 <= i < n-1), and each a_{t+1} is obtained from a_t by choosing an index i < n-1 with L'[i] = 0 and a_t[i] - a_t[i+1] = 1, then swapping a_t[i] and a_t[i+1]. The function returns a result r, and: if at least one unlocking mask L' makes Sortable(nums,L') true, then r is the minimum, over all such L', of the number of indices i with locked[i] = 1 and L'[i] = 0; if no unlocking mask makes Sortable(nums,L') true, then r = -1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1; len(locked) = n; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 3 and locked[i] is 0 or 1.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or go out of bounds on any input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1; len(locked) = n; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 3 and locked[i] is 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, either r = -1, or 0 <= r <= n.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1; len(locked) = n; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 3 and locked[i] is 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns r and r >= 0, r is at most the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and locked[i] = 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1; len(locked) = n; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 3 and locked[i] is 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r = -1 if and only if there exist indices i and j with 0 <= i < j < n, nums[i] = 3, and nums[j] = 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1; len(locked) = n; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 3 and locked[i] is 0 or 1.

statement: The function returns 0 if there do not exist indices i and j with 0 <= i < j < n, nums[i] = 3, and nums[j] = 1; otherwise the function returns -1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1; len(locked) = n; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 3 and locked[i] = 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns r and r >= 0, r = 0 if and only if nums is sortable with the original mask locked, i.e., there is a finite sequence of allowed adjacent swaps using locked[i] = 0 as the permission condition that transforms nums into a nondecreasing array.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1; len(locked) = n; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 3 and locked[i] is 0 or 1.

statement: The function returns r equal to the number of indices i such that 0 <= i < n, locked[i] = 1, and i is in R.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1; len(locked) = n; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 3 and locked[i] is 0 or 1; there do not exist indices i and j with 0 <= i < j < n, nums[i] = 3, and nums[j] = 1. Let last1 be the largest index j with nums[j] = 1, or -1 if there is none. Let p1 be the smallest index i with nums[i] = 2 for which some j > i has nums[j] = 1, or n if there is no such i. Let last2 be the largest index j with nums[j] = 2, or -1 if there is none. Let p2 be the smallest index i with nums[i] = 3 for which some j > i has nums[j] = 2, or n if there is no such i. Let R = { i | 0 <= i < n and ( (p1 <= i and i < last1) or (p2 <= i and i < last2) ) }.

statement: Let r1 be the result of the function on (nums,locked1) and r2 be the result on (nums,locked2). Whenever both calls return results, either r1 = r2 = -1, or r1 >= 0, r2 >= 0, and r2 <= r1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 3. Let locked1 and locked2 be length-n binary masks. Assume locked2[i] <= locked1[i] for every 0 <= i < n, so locked2 is at least as unlocked as locked1 at every index.

statement: If the function returns r1 on (nums,locked1) and r2 on (nums,locked2), then r1 = r2, and this common value is the number of indices i in R with locked1[i] = 1 (equivalently, the number with locked2[i] = 1).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 3; there do not exist indices i and j with 0 <= i < j < n, nums[i] = 3, and nums[j] = 1. Let last1 be the largest index j with nums[j] = 1, or -1 if there is none. Let p1 be the smallest index i with nums[i] = 2 for which some j > i has nums[j] = 1, or n if there is no such i. Let last2 be the largest index j with nums[j] = 2, or -1 if there is none. Let p2 be the smallest index i with nums[i] = 3 for which some j > i has nums[j] = 2, or n if there is no such i. Let R = { i | 0 <= i < n and ( (p1 <= i and i < last1) or (p2 <= i and i < last2) ) }. Let locked1 and locked2 be length-n binary masks that agree on every index in R, i.e., locked1[i] = locked2[i] for every i in R.
